The Minnesota Department of Education voluntarily removed its stop-pay on Feeding Our Future's federal meal-program reimbursement claims on April 30, 2021. No court ordered the resumption. The Minnesota Judicial Branch issued a public correction stating Judge John Guthmann never ordered MDE to resume payments, and the court's own June 24, 2021 written order independently confirms this: it denies Feeding Our Future's motion to force an end to the stop-pay as moot, “because MDE lifted its stop pay ... and paid the reimbursement claims that were the subject of the motion.” At a hearing that same day, MDE's attorney told the court on the record that the stop-pay was no longer being enforced and that claims were expected to be scheduled for payment the following week.

supporting_passages.quote: Feeding Our Future’s Motion and Renewed Motion for a Temporary Restraining Order seeking an Order requiring MDE to end its “stop pay” policy as to Feeding Our Future and to timely pay Feeding Our Future’s claims is denied as moot because MDE lifted its “stop pay” as to Feeding Our Future’s claims and paid the reimbursement claims that were the subject of the motion.
MDE is not claiming and is not continuing the stop pay on ... Feeding Our Future’s claims.

qualifiers: MDE's decision to remove the stop-pay is distinct from the exact date every reimbursement dollar was actually received; the April 30 hearing transcript records MDE's attorney saying claims were expected to show as scheduled for payment the following Thursday or Friday, not that they had already been paid that day.

A congressional interview of then-MDE Assistant Commissioner Daron Korte adds that MDE's internal decision also involved Monica Herrera and Emily Honer, that then-Commissioner Heather Mueller was informed rather than asked to approve, and that MDE's Attorney General litigating attorneys were involved. Korte was later named personally as a defendant in Feeding Our Future's civil complaint — relevant context for weighing his account, though it has independently checked out against the primary court record on every point verified here.
This is an oversight-and-compliance record, not a fraud finding against MDE. MDE is not charged with fraud anywhere in this corpus.

claims.claim_text: On June 24, 2021, Ramsey County District Court Judge John Guthmann found the Minnesota Department of Education in civil contempt of a December 22, 2020 stipulated order requiring MDE to promptly process Feeding Our Future's site applications — a separate issue from the reimbursement stop-pay, which the same order resolved as moot. The court ordered MDE to pay Feeding Our Future a $35,750 contempt sanction plus $11,750 in stipulated attorneys' fees, a combined $47,500.

supporting_passages.quote: Feeding Our Future’s motions to find MDE in contempt of the stipulated December 22, 2020 Order (“Order”) is granted. The Court finds MDE’s violation of the Order sanctionable and hereby orders MDE to pay Feeding Our Future $35,750.

As part of the ruling on the motions for contempt, MDE is also ordered to pay Feeding Our Future’s reasonable attorneys’ fees for pursuing its motions for contempt of court in the amount of $11,750, which was stipulated by the parties.

amounts.methodology: Civil contempt sanction ordered for MDE's violation of the December 22, 2020 stipulated order.
Stipulated attorneys' fees ordered alongside the contempt sanction, for pursuing the contempt motions.
Sum of the $35,750 sanction and $11,750 attorneys' fees ordered in the same paragraph of the same order. Do not add this total to its two components again.

qualifiers: This sanction concerns MDE's delay processing Feeding Our Future's site applications under a December 22, 2020 order — not the reimbursement stop-pay, which the same order separately resolved as moot because MDE had already voluntarily lifted it.
This is a civil contempt sanction against a state agency for a compliance failure, not a criminal or fraud finding.
